subject: SIG follow-up: Clarifying Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployment differences
messages:
From: Sylvia Price <sylvia.price@acme-fin.com>

Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme-fin.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SIG questionnaire — deployment mode questions

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for sending over the SIG. We're working through the workbook and have a few follow-ups specifically around deployment modes. The security team at Acme needs a short, clear explanation for the SIG on three points: Hosted (Redwood-managed), Dedicated (Redwood-dedicated capacity), and Private (VPC/on-prem).

Can you confirm for each mode:
- Where customer data (model input and outputs, KV cache) resides and how long it's retained
- Who controls the control plane and encryption keys (customer vs Redwood)
- Whether SOC 2 scope and other evidence (audit logs, vulnerability scanning) apply the same way across modes or differ

If you have a short annex or diagram you can attach that would be great — our reviewers prefer something concise to include with the SIG responses.

Targeting an internal review on Tue so if we can get something by EOD Mon (your time) that would help.

Best,
Sylvia
Security Compliance Manager
Acme Financial

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sylvia Price <sylvia.price@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme-fin.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire — deployment mode questions

Hi Sylvia — thanks for the clear list. Attached is a short annex that lays out the differences and a VPC diagram. Below is a concise summary you can paste into the SIG. If you'd like, we can also join a 30-min call tomorrow to walk your reviewers through it.

Summary (short):
- Hosted (Redwood-managed): Control plane, model serving, and KV caches are hosted in Redwood's multi-tenant environment. Data-in-transit is encrypted TLS; data-at-rest is encrypted with keys managed by Redwood KMS by default. SOC 2 controls and our SOC 2 report cover the hosted environment; access to the report can be provided via secure link. Retention for request logs and KV cache aligns with customer-configured session TTLs (default short-lived) and Redwood retention policy; we do not use customer data to train models.

- Dedicated (Redwood-dedicated capacity): Compute (GPU pools) and runtime instances are dedicated to your account but remain in Redwood-managed infrastructure. Network isolation and tenancy isolation are enforced; encryption is the same as Hosted. SOC 2 applies to the underlying infrastructure; some operational controls (e.g., physical access, host-level controls) remain with Redwood. You can request dedicated key-wrapping options for greater isolation.

- Private (VPC / on-prem): Full private deployments where the control plane and/or serving runtime are inside a customer VPC or on-premises. Customer-managed KMS is supported (bring-your-own-key), and network egress is configurable/air-gapped. In this mode, certain operational responsibilities (host patching, physical security for on-prem) transfer to the customer; Redwood provides the same software and audit hooks. SOC 2 evidence for the Redwood software is available, but infrastructure evidence will differ if fully customer-hosted.

I've attached: SIG_Redwood_Deployment_Annex.pdf (one-page summary + table), network_diagram_vpc.png, and a short note about how to request the SOC 2 report.

If that works, I'll update the SIG workbook with these verbatim answers and mark items where we can provide evidence links.

Cheers,
Monica
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): SIG_Redwood_Deployment_Annex.pdf, network_diagram_vpc.png

Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire — deployment mode questions (technical details)

Hi Tom — quick answers from the infra side:
- KV cache: In Hosted we primarily keep KV cache in host memory attached to the serving process (ephemeral) with optional short-lived managed Redis for specific use-cases; no long-term persistence unless explicitly enabled. In Dedicated, KV cache is still in-process/host memory by default and can be configured to back to a dedicated Redis instance within the same isolated tenancy if you want persistence across restarts. For Private (VPC/on-prem) the KV cache behaviour is under the customer's control — we can run the cache inside your VPC and configure persistence policies to your requirements.
- Key rotation & CMK: Dedicated supports customer-managed key wrapping (bring-your-own-key) via key wrapping with your KMS; you can rotate CMKs on your cadence (monthly) — Redwood supports key rotation workflows and will rewrap persisted secrets accordingly. For Hosted, key management is Redwood-managed by default but BYOK options exist for higher tiers.

I dropped a short runbook link below with the exact config flags and API endpoints: https://redwood.example.com/internal/runbooks/kv-cache-and-keys (we'll provide a sanitized link for your SIG attachments).

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Hi Sylvia / Tom —

Following up with a few compliance points so you can close the SIG items:
- SOC 2: Our SOC 2 report covers Redwood's hosted and dedicated offerings where infrastructure is Redwood-managed. For Private/on-prem deployments, the SOC 2 report covers the Redwood application and related software controls, but infrastructure-level evidence (physical security, host patching) will be specific to your environment. We can provide the SOC 2 report via the secure link included in the annex (soc2_access_instructions.txt).
- Audit logs & retention: Hosted/Dedicated: audit logs (API access, admin actions) are retained per contract; default 90 days, extendable. Private: logs can be forwarded to your SIEM or kept locally per your retention policy.
- Evidence delivery: We can deliver SIG completed workbook entries, a signed attest letter, network diagram, and a secure link to SOC 2. For high-sensitivity requests, we can arrange an in-person or remote audit review (redwood security lead + your auditors).

If you confirm what evidence package you want attached to the SIG (quick package: workbook + annex + SOC 2 link) we'll transmit that today.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Director, Legal & Compliance
Redwood Inference
